title: Reworking Groove Me for King Floyd without the producer's knowledge
summary: He fixes raw songs with changes; Groove Me was arranged on the way from hotel to studio, cut without King Floyd present, and he got no percentage.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, when you, when you get a song and you get it by inexperienced people, you have to do some changes because the changes are raw, you know, it's not really put together as such. It's got a little form to it but changes why the guys, the guys that rolled it, there was a musician and a piano player, Joe Broussard, the piano player, he was limited in his chord structure, you know. So you hear things like that and you say, well let's try this and let's try that, you know, and that's how that is. The same way with the song.
So Groove Me by King Floyd?

That was the same thing. As a matter of fact, when we did Groove Me by King Floyd, Floyd wasn't there. And they didn't even know if I was gonna, if I, that's what I was saying about producers before. The producer had one song, I think that was the song on the back of Groove Me, whatever that was. It's only, it was one of the songs that was a hit after Groove Me. And the producer told me, he said, listen man, do any songs on all of these tunes that's on the tape but, you have to do this certain tune that I want. So they didn't even know I was doing, uh, uh, uh, Groove Me. And by the way, I did the Groove Me, uh, on the, from the hotel to the, from the hotel to the studio is when I did the arrangement. But, so when you say you're doing an arrangement like that, I've been playing with the song so much that it was in me anyway what the arrangements can do.
You're thinking of bass, drums, horns, everything. I'm thinking about everything. So you're saying when you cut that, King Floyd wasn't even around?

Uh-uh. They didn't even know I was gonna cut it. See that's what I was saying about being a producer and being an executive producer, that's two different things. But, the concept for people in New Orleans is that when you put out the, put out the money, you're the producer, you know. And it's not that way of a wild. But, in this particular case, the cat did get me, he had a call, and he said if we get a hit out of any of these tunes, I'll give you this call. And so, I got a call after he beat it up.
On Groove Me? Yeah. You didn't, you didn't get any percentage on Groove Me? No.
